why:
phase-482 W4 (2026-10-07): on `rclcpp_lifecycle::LifecycleNode` this returns `const State&` (`get_current_state`: `State`), as upstream's does, so a ported call site's use of the result compiles unchanged.

Before phase-482 W4: LANDED 2026-09-06 (PR #602, issue 1099 archived), gap -> divergence. `trigger_transition(uint8_t)` now takes `lifecycle_msgs/msg/Transition` ids -- the same numbers rclcpp means -- and `nros_core::lifecycle`, `RCLC_LIFECYCLE_TRANSITION_*` and the wire path all share that numbering; `shutdown()` resolves its id from the CURRENT state via `shutdown_transition_for`. What REMAINS, and is the divergence this row now records: (1) an ours-only overload `trigger_transition(LifecycleTransition)` on a closed `enum class` (the preferred, type-safe spelling; rclcpp's second overload takes a `lifecycle_msgs::msg::Transition` OBJECT, see `cpp:Transition`), and (2) ids `0` (`TRANSITION_CREATE`) and `8` (`TRANSITION_DESTROY`) return `InvalidArgument` where rclcpp would perform them -- a node in a fixed arena is created and destroyed with the image, so clause 1 binds there and the refusal is loud. Everything below is the record as written BEFORE the fix, kept as the history of the finding.

phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. Issue 1099, then open. The RANKED-1 finding of the sweep: our name, our arity, our parameter type, and a DIFFERENT id space.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclcpp_lifecycle::LifecycleNode::trigger_transition(uint8_t id)` takes an id from `lifecycle_msgs/msg/Transition` — 1 CONFIGURE, 2 CLEANUP, 3 ACTIVATE, 4 DEACTIVATE, 5/6/7 the three shutdowns, 8 DESTROY. Those constants are the ROS 2 wire vocabulary; a ported file that reaches for the raw overload is reaching for them.

OURS: `packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp_lifecycle/lifecycle_node.hpp:173` passes the caller's byte straight to `nros_cpp_lifecycle_change_state`, which resolves it with `LifecycleTransition::from_u8` — our INTERNAL enum (`packages/core/nros-core/src/lifecycle.rs`), where 2 is Activate, 3 Deactivate, 4 Cleanup and 8 ErrorRecovery. Four of eight ids differ. The five named helpers above it (`configure`/`activate`/`deactivate`/`cleanup`/`shutdown`) are correct precisely because they are written in the internal space.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: SILENTLY WRONG, in the worst direction the campaign has measured. `trigger_transition(2)` on an Inactive node ACTIVATES it and returns `Result::ok` where ROS 2 would clean it up. Nothing about a fixed arena requires a different numbering, so clause 1 does not bind and the disposition is ADOPT: route the raw overload through the mapping that already exists in-tree at `packages/core/nros-node/src/lifecycle_services.rs` (`transition_id`, `from_msg_transition_id`, `to_msg_transition`) — which is used on the WIRE path only, so `ros2 lifecycle set` and the C++ API disagree about the same node today.

SIBLING, same row because it is the same defect: `LifecycleNode::shutdown()` (`rclcpp_lifecycle/lifecycle_node.hpp:164`) hardcodes id 5 = ShutdownUnconfigured, whose only legal source state is Unconfigured, so it cannot shut down an Inactive or Active node; our own Rust state machine resolves the shutdown transition from the CURRENT state and the header bypasses it.

WHY THE GATE COULD NOT SEE IT: `scripts/api_parity/correlate.py` never compares return types or enum discriminants — when arities intersect and no rule fires it assigns `same` unconditionally — so this row correlates `same` and was UNLEDGERED until now. Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.
